newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates pinned up above repo rate.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates pinned up above repo rate.

text.p: German call money was trading steady from Friday at around 3.05/10 percent on Monday, with most transactions taking place at 3.07/08 percent.
Dealers said continued speculation about possible changes in the Bundesbank's securities repurchase rate policy was buoying rates, holding them above the three percent repo rate.

But many traders were sceptical of an early move by the central bank to free up or raise the rate, arguing that this would be bad for the economy and was unlikely to have the desired effect of stopping the dollar's surge against the mark.
But forward rates also hinted at speculation that a moderate rate move was seen in the pipeline. One-month rates stood at 3.10/15 and three-month rates at 3.18/23 perent.
Dealers said a drain of funds from the market due to transfer payments made at the start of the month was expected to by offset by Tuesday, when payments would start to be booked to accounts.

They nonetheless expected a small addition of funds to the market in this week's securities repurchase tender. One trader said he expected up to one billion marks to be added to the market in the pact, already announced at a three percent rate.
Banks held 41.2 billion marks in reserve accounts at the central bank on Friday for an average of 41.2 billion marks for the first three days of the month.

Banks took up about 200 million marks at the 4.50 percent Lombard emergency funding rate on Friday, down from 4.3 billion on Thursday, when borrowing was boosted as banks sought funds to top up reserve requirements for July.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was calculated at 3.09455 percent on Monday, down slightly from 3.09580.
